summary:
Vesta turns NASA’s microgravity fire research into clear, usable fire-safety insights for crews living beyond Earth. We built an interactive, AI-powered web platform on 24 investigations from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository, covering 1,807 tests, plus related NASA technical reports.

Users can explore and compare experiments, read plain-language or expert summaries, and rank studies by relevance to a spacecraft, the ISS, a Moon base, a Mars base, or a pressurized rover. Insights are organized around preventing, detecting, and putting out fires. An Ask AI assistant answers questions with cited sources, and an experimental machine-learning model trained on NASA FLEX data estimates whether a burning fuel droplet will go out on its own. Clean data downloads support further modeling, and a Gaps view shows what hasn’t been tested yet, such as fires in partial gravity or solid materials at the higher oxygen levels planned for Moon bases.

This matters because fire behaves differently in space, and a crew can’t simply evacuate. Vesta makes years of NASA research easy to find, compare, and act on as humanity returns to the Moon.
details:
WHAT VESTA DOES

Vesta is an AI-powered web platform that makes NASA's microgravity fire research easy to find, compare and understand, so it can inform fire safety for spacecraft, space stations, Moon and Mars bases, and pressurized rovers. It brings together 24 investigations from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository (19 flown in space, 5 ground studies), covering 1,807 tests, plus NASA technical reports and NASA's official challenge resources.

LINKS

Live site: [LIVE SITE URL]GitHub repository: [GITHUB REPO URL]Launch video: [VIDEO TUTORIAL]

Users can:

  • Explore all 24 studies and open a profile for each: goal, fuels, test conditions, sensors, results and their safety meaning, with sources.
  • Plan a mission: rank studies by how well their test conditions match a spacecraft, the ISS, a Moon base, a Mars base or a pressurized rover.
  • Compare 2–3 studies side by side, with an AI-written explanation.
  • Read fire-safety insights grouped by preventing, detecting and putting out fires, plus equipment notes.
  • See the gaps: no partial-gravity data yet, and no solid materials tested at the 30%+ oxygen planned for Moon bases.
  • Ask questions in plain language and get answers with cited NASA sources.
  • Try an experimental machine-learning model that estimates whether a burning fuel droplet will go out on its own, shown on a map of real NASA tests.
  • Download the cleaned test data (CSV and JSON) for their own modeling.
  • Learn the basics through a 10-chapter interactive journey and hands-on explainers, and see how this research helps firefighters on Earth.

HOW IT WORKS

  1. Data prep (Python): we cleaned every PSI test table into one consistent dataset, fixing errors such as mislabeled columns and spreadsheet glitches, and computed all key numbers in code.
  2. Saved AI answers: free models on OpenRouter (Baidu ERNIE 5.5 Flash and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL) wrote study summaries, insights and ranking reasons from the source documents. Super VL also read scanned pages. Every number in AI-written text was automatically checked against its source.
  3. Rankings: scores are computed in code from each study's oxygen, pressure, gravity and fuel type. AI only explains them.
  4. Ask AI: keyword search finds the best NASA passages, and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL answers with citations. If our sources don't cover a question, it says so instead of guessing.
  5. Prediction model: a logistic regression trained on 261 FLEX tests. It's right 84% of the time in testing (balanced accuracy 78%), compared with 69% for always guessing "the flame goes out."

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Vesta turns years of scattered NASA data into answers that engineers, researchers, professors and students can use in minutes. It helps mission planners see which experiments matter for their habitat, shows researchers where new experiments are most needed, and gives students a clear, trustworthy way to learn how fire behaves in space. Our goal is to help keep crews safe as humanity returns to the Moon.

TOOLS

Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Bun; Netlify (hosting and serverless functions); Python with PyMuPDF, scikit-learn and Jupyter; OpenRouter (Baidu ERNIE 5.5 Flash, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL); Claude Code for development assistance; GitHub; Archivo and Atkinson Hyperlegible fonts (Google Fonts). The logo was made with an AI image tool and is labeled as AI-generated.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

  • The name: "Vesta" is the Roman goddess of the hearth (the home fire) and the asteroid NASA's Dawn spacecraft orbited. We're guarding the fire in the first homes beyond Earth.
  • A signature flame that switches from an Earth teardrop to the round blue ball fire becomes in microgravity.
  • A story-driven journey, interactive physics explainers, and a "living flame" that shrinks as the model's chance of the flame going out rises.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

  • Accuracy and trust: sources on every claim, numbers computed in code, an automatic number check on AI text, and flags where a table and a report disagree.
  • Honesty: a dedicated view of what NASA's data doesn't cover yet, and clear "AI-written" and "experimental model" labels.
  • Audience: plain-language and expert modes, accessible design (keyboard use, reduced motion, high contrast), and light and dark themes.
  • Cost and reliability: free tiers, static pages, and saved answers that still work if the AI service is busy.
  • Rights: only NASA and PSI content is published, with no NASA logos and AI-generated images watermarked.
